# console-chat — a chat panel driven by a running Claude Code session

## Problem

Ops staff work the console by clicking through payments, disputes, and payouts. The ask: a chat
window docked on the right-hand side that answers questions and performs the console's basic
operations in natural language — "show me disputed payments for Brandt & Sohn", "what was
yesterday's captured volume", "give me a CSV of last week's refunds without card numbers".

**Constraint that decides the architecture:** there is no API billing. The chat must run on a
**Claude Code process under the developer's existing login** — "this session" — not the Messages
API.

## Interpretation (v2, corrected)

The web route spawns **headless Claude Code**: `claude -p <turn> --output-format stream-json`,
with the merchant console directory as its cwd, so it loads the same `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules`,
skills, and agents this session has — a session *like this one*, on the same model, same login.
Conversation continuity across HTTP turns is `--resume <session_id>`; the first turn of a chat
creates a session, every later turn resumes it (which also reuses the prompt cache).

**Proven before planning, on this machine (2026-09-09):** a nested child process
`claude -p "…" --output-format json` under the current login returned `HEADLESS_OK`, a
`session_id`, model `claude-fable-5-1`, `provider: firstParty`, `permission_denials: []`. Installed
CLI is 2.1.267 and has every flag below. It does **not** have `--max-turns`; the runner enforces its
own wall-clock limit.

**Why not tmux.** `tmux send-keys` into an interactive `claude` plus `capture-pane` scraping was the
literal reading. It loses to `-p --output-format stream-json`, which is the same process with
structured NDJSON events, a returned `session_id`, no TUI to parse, and no permission prompt that
can hang with nobody at the keyboard. Same login, same capabilities, machine-readable.

**Optional literal reading.** `CHAT_RESUME_SESSION=<id>` lets the route resume one specific
existing session (this one, say) as the base of every chat instead of starting fresh. Caveats
stated on CHAT4: every web turn appends to that transcript, two concurrent chats would race on
one session, and a 1M-token session is slow to resume. Default is fresh-per-chat.

## Current state (verified, with paths — all under `build-battle/merchant-console/`)

- `src/app/layout.tsx:71-83` — shell is `SidebarProvider > AppSidebar + div.w-full > header + main`.
  No right-hand column; the panel needs a flex row here and nowhere else.
- `src/components/Sidebar.tsx` — `"use client"`, context + cookie-persisted open state
  (`sidebar:state`, lines 19-20). The chat panel mirrors this pattern.
- `src/components/Drawer.tsx`, `Button.tsx`, `Input.tsx`, `Badge.tsx` — Tremor primitives to reuse.
  No Dialog/Checkbox/Textarea primitive; native controls with Tailwind are the precedent (NWP-101).
- `src/app/api/payments/route.ts`, `src/app/api/payments/export/route.ts` — the only two routes,
  both via `parseFilters`. The error shape is `NextResponse.json({ message }, { status })`.
- **The store is in memory inside the Next.js process** (`src/data/store.ts`). A spawned Claude
  process cannot read it directly. Its bridge to live data is the app's own HTTP routes over
  loopback — `curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/payments?status=disputed` — plus `Read`/`Grep` on
  the source for "how does X work" questions.
- `src/data/metrics.ts` carries the NWP-102 defects. Nothing here fixes them.
- `package.json` — no new dependency is needed: `child_process` is Node. `vitest` 3, node
  environment, `src/**/*.test.ts` only — `.tsx` cannot be unit-tested.
- No `.env*` file; `.gitignore` already ignores `.env*`. Dev server binds `127.0.0.1` only.

## Domain rules that bind every card

| Rule | Source | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validate everything from the client against an allowlist | `api-routes.md` | The chat turn text, `sessionId` (UUID shape), and `context` are client input; validated before a process is spawned. The turn text is passed as an **argument**, never interpolated into a shell string. |
| Never return a full card number | `api-routes.md`, `cards.md` | The routes already mask; the operating guide forbids reading `src/data/generate.ts` output into answers. |
| Same error shape everywhere | `api-routes.md` | `{ message }` with an honest status; 503 when `claude` is missing or not logged in. |
| Dialogs and forms must be operable; Tailwind only | `components.md` | Panel has an accessible name, the composer a label, Escape closes, focus returns. |
| No DB, no persistence | `CLAUDE.md` | No chat history stored by the app. Claude Code's own session transcript is the continuity; the client keeps a display transcript. |
| **The route is a remote shell into a Claude process** | this plan | Tool policy is load-bearing: `--disallowedTools Edit Write NotebookEdit`, `--allowedTools` limited to `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, and `Bash(curl:*)`; loopback-only app binding; a per-session lock; a wall-clock kill. Documented in `README.md` as a local-dev feature, not a deployable one. |

## Architecture

```
ChatPanel (client) --POST /api/chat {text, sessionId?, context}--> route.ts (CHAT4)
    request.ts validates → sessions.ts takes the per-session lock →
    runner.ts (CHAT2) spawns:
      claude -p <text> --output-format stream-json --verbose
             [--resume <sessionId>] --permission-mode <policy>
             --allowedTools Read Grep Glob "Bash(curl:*)"
             --disallowedTools Edit Write NotebookEdit
             --append-system-prompt-file src/lib/chat/console.md   (CHAT3)
      cwd = build-battle/merchant-console ; env CHAT_APP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3000
    NDJSON events → typed events (events.ts) → SSE to the panel
    <-- text {delta} | tool_call {name, input} | tool_result {name, summary} | done {sessionId} | error {message}
```

- **Request contract** (CHAT4): `{ text: string (1..4000), sessionId?: string (UUID), context?: { pathname, search } }`.
  History is not sent — the resumed session holds it.
- **Event contract** (CHAT2 defines the types in `src/lib/chat/events.ts`; CHAT4 emits; CHAT5 renders):
  `text`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `done` (carries the `sessionId` the client must send next), `error`.
- **Process contract** (CHAT2): one child per turn; killed on client abort or at `CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS`
  (default 120000); stderr captured into the `error` event message, never into the page.
- **Model:** whatever the login's default is (the proof ran on `claude-fable-5-1`); `--model` is
  passed only if `CHAT_MODEL` is set.

## Basic operations in scope

The session performs them with its own tools, guided by `console.md`:

| Ask | How the session does it |
| --- | --- |
| Find / filter payments | `curl $CHAT_APP_ORIGIN/api/payments?status=…&merchantId=…&search=…` |
| One payment, its refunds and dispute | `curl …/api/payments?search=<id>`; `Read src/data/queries.ts` when asked how |
| Daily volume | `curl` is not enough (no metrics route) — the guide says to answer from `src/data/metrics.ts` and to state NWP-102's known defects |
| CSV export link | compose `/api/payments/export?status=…&columns=…&scope=…` (NWP-101 params); no `last4` unless asked |
| "How does X work" | `Read`/`Grep` the source; cite paths |

**Out of scope, deliberately:** write actions (refund, freeze, issue card) — no such routes exist;
persisting chat history; auth; multi-user isolation beyond the per-session lock; deploying this
anywhere but a developer's machine.

## Verification (end to end, after wave 2)

1. `cd build-battle/merchant-console && npm test && npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit` — green.
2. `scripts/chat-smoke.sh` (CHAT3) passes against the running dev server: a headless turn answers
   "how many disputed payments?" with the number `/api/payments?status=disputed` reports, via a
   `Bash(curl:*)` tool call, with `permission_denials: []`.
3. `curl -N -X POST 127.0.0.1:3000/api/chat -d '{"text":"How many disputed payments does Brandt & Sohn have?"}'`
   streams `tool_call` (Bash curl), `tool_result`, text with the right count, then `done {sessionId}`.
   A second POST with that `sessionId` and `"and how many of those are over €300?"` answers in
   context (proves `--resume`).
4. A POST with `text` of 5,000 chars, or `sessionId: "../x"`, or a `system` key → 400 `{ message }`.
   With `CHAT_CLAUDE_BIN=/nonexistent` → 503 `{ message }`, no hang.
5. Ask "delete the seed file" → the answer says it cannot (Edit/Write disallowed); `git status` clean.
6. Browser: panel toggles, survives reload, Escape closes; "what am I looking at?" on
   `/payments?status=disputed` answers using `context`.

## Risks

- **It is a shell.** Anyone who can POST to the route runs `curl` and reads the repo as you.
  Mitigations are structural (loopback binding, tool allow/deny lists, no writes) and documented;
  the README says "local development only" in the first line of the section.
- **No `--max-turns` in 2.1.267.** A runaway tool loop is bounded only by `CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS`. The
  runner kills the process group, not just the child, so a spawned `curl` dies with it.
- **Usage, not dollars.** Each fresh session loads ~20k tokens of repo context (measured); the
  subscription meters usage. `--resume` reuses the 1h prompt cache; the panel keeps one session per
  chat rather than one per turn.
- **Nested-spawn guard.** The proof ran with `CLAUDECODE` unset from a parent Claude session. The
  runner always clears `CLAUDECODE` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` in the child env.
- **Auth.** The authentication docs state that in `-p` mode the `/login` subscription credential is
  used automatically when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, with no usage restriction stated
  (`code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md`). CHAT4's README paragraph says so and links it.
- **Docs vs. installed binary.** The CLI reference lists `--max-turns`; 2.1.267's `--help` does
  not have it. The docs say `--verbose` is optional for stream-json; without it only `result`
  lines appear, so the runner always passes it. Where they disagree, the binary wins.
- **Vitest cannot test `.tsx`.** CHAT1/CHAT5 acceptance is `tsc` + lint + a rendered-page check;
  CHAT2/3/4 carry the tested logic, with a fake `claude` binary so no test spawns the real one.

## Open questions

- Fresh session per chat (default) vs. `CHAT_RESUME_SESSION` pinning one base session — decide when
  the panel is usable; both are supported by CHAT4.
- Whether to expose `Read` at all, or make the session curl-only. Default: allow `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob`
  so "how does X work" answers cite code; drop them if the chat should only ever see data.
- The docs say the Claude Agent SDK (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) can also use the CLI's
  subscription login. If that holds up in practice, CHAT2 could shrink to an SDK wrapper instead
  of a hand-rolled spawn + NDJSON parser, at the cost of one dependency. The spawn path is the one
  proven on this machine, so it ships first; revisit after wave 1.
